rows.question: Which company built the spacecraft Michael Collins stayed in while the first Moon landing took place?
rows.answer: Michael Collins stayed in the command module Columbia during the Apollo 11 landing [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)". rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
Before launch, the heaters of oxygen tank No. 2 were run on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in that tank. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The cause was the tank's thermostatic switches. Their heater specification was revised to 65 volts in 1965, but the switches were not changed. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The board's report called the switch failure "a serious oversight in which all parties share." [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

rows.question: The landing site described in the Apollo 11 Mission Report's powered-descent section was named by an astronaut. What was first about the Gemini flight he commanded, and when was it?
rows.answer:
The landing site is Tranquility Base. Neil Armstrong named it at touchdown [[tranquility-base]] "[stated] Named by Neil Armstrong at touchdown: Houston, Tranquility Base here, the Eagle has landed (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

The powered-descent section of the Apollo 11 Mission Report covers the landing point. Its description reads "Section 5.3, pages 5-4 to 5-6: five computer alarms, crater avoidance, manual control, landing point and propellant use" [[apollo-11-mission-report-ch-05]] description: "Section [unverified] 5.3, pages 5-4 to 5-6: five computer alarms, crater avoidance, manual control, landing point and propellant use". One of its facts gives the landing point: "[stated] Manual control began at about 600 feet and the craft landed about 1100 feet downrange of the initial aim point (src: Apollo 11 Mission Report p.5-5, 2026-10-24)" [[apollo-11-mission-report-ch-05]].

Armstrong commanded Gemini 8 in 1966, and that flight was the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit [[neil-armstrong]] "[stated] Earlier commanded Gemini 8 in 1966, the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)".

The brain gives only the year, 1966, so the exact date of the Gemini 8 flight is not in the notes.

rows.question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?
rows.answer:
The astronaut who caught the measles was Charlie Duke, the backup lunar module pilot. He caught German measles from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch [[charlie-duke]] "[stated] Caught German measles from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". His exposure started the crew swap [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Backup lunar module pilot Charlie Duke caught German measles and exposed the crews (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)".

The swap brought in Jack Swigert, who became Apollo 13's prime command module pilot, changed from backup on 1970-04-10 [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Apollo 13 role is prime command module pilot (was backup command module pilot, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)".

Swigert later was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982, but died before taking office [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)". The brain does not say when or how he died.

rows.question: The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was carried by a spacecraft. Which Apollo 11 crew member piloted that kind of spacecraft, and what did he do during the landing?
rows.answer:
The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was Oxygen tank No. 2. Its note describes it as "Apollo 13 service module tank whose 28-volt thermostatic switches failed under 65-volt power and caused the explosion" [[oxygen-tank-2]] description (frontmatter).

The command and service module carried the oxygen tanks: "Its service module carried the oxygen tanks that supplied power and air (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)" [[command-service-module]].

Michael Collins was the Apollo 11 command module pilot: "Command module pilot of Apollo 11 (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)" [[michael-collins]].

During the landing, Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia: "Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)" [[michael-collins]].

The notes do not say more about what Collins did during the landing itself.

rows.question: How many years separate Neil Armstrong's Gemini 8 command and John Young's command of the first Space Shuttle flight?
rows.answer: Neil Armstrong commanded Gemini 8 in 1966 [[neil-armstrong]] "[stated] Earlier commanded Gemini 8 in 1966, the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)". John Young commanded STS-1, the first Space Shuttle flight, in 1981 [[john-young]] "[stated] Commanded STS-1 in 1981, the first Space Shuttle flight (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)". The gap between the two is 15 years.

rows.question: How long did the Apollo 11 crew spend on the lunar surface?
rows.answer:
The brain does not say how long the Apollo 11 crew spent on the lunar surface. It gives the landing and splashdown dates, but not the length of the surface stay itself. The Eagle landed on 1969-07-20 ([[apollo-11]] "[stated] Lunar module Eagle landed on 1969-07-20 in the Sea of Tranquility (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"). Neil Armstrong first stepped onto the surface on 1969-07-21 UTC ([[neil-armstrong]] "[stated] First person to step onto the lunar surface on 1969-07-21 UTC (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"). The crew splashed down in the Pacific on 1969-07-24 ([[apollo-11]] "[stated] Splashed down in the Pacific on 1969-07-24 (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)").

Those dates span the whole mission, not the time on the surface. Missing: the moment the crew left the surface, or a stated duration for the surface stay. The Mission Report section in the brain covers only the powered descent (pages 5-4 to 5-6), so it does not give that either.

rows.question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?
rows.answer:
The "mailbox" was the Apollo 13 CO2 scrubber adapter. It was improvised because the command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's receptacles were round. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

It was made from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] Engineers devised an adapter from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

Engineers at Mission Control in Houston devised it. [[mission-control-houston]] "[stated] Engineers there devised the Apollo 13 carbon dioxide scrubber adapter (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The crew built it from radioed instructions. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The crew built it from radioed instructions (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The notes don't give the step-by-step construction or the exact dimensions.

rows.question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
rows.answer:
Here are the 1970 dates the brain records for Apollo 13, in order. I've corrected the citations to copy each fact line in full, including its `[stated]` tag.

1. **1970-04-06:** Blood tests from the physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

2. **1970-04-10:** The crew swap was decided and announced, and Jack Swigert replaced Ken Mattingly as command module pilot. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

3. **1970-04-11:** Apollo 13 launched. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

4. **1970-04-13:** Oxygen tank No. 2 exploded, about 56 hours into the flight. The same day, a Mission Control abort decision changed the goal from a lunar landing at Fra Mauro to a safe return to Earth. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)". [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

5. **1970-04-17:** The crew, using the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat, splashed down. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

6. **June 1970:** The Apollo 13 Review Board report was published. The board, chaired by Edgar Cortright, traced the explosion to a fire in tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The brain gives only the month for the review board report, so no exact day is recorded for it.
